small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs targeting this shape (C_OUT=64, HW_OUT=254*254≈64516, C_IN=8, KH=KW=3): try `BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_HW=256, num_warps=8, num_stages=2/3` and `BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_HW=512, num_warps=8`. With C_OUT=64 a single OC tile of 64 eliminates the OC grid dimension and keeps weights resident.
- Reorder the inner loops to `ic` outermost, then `kh`, `kw`: pre-load all 9 weight values per `(oc, ic)` once and reuse them across spatial loads, reducing redundant `tl.load`s of weights from 72 to 72 but enabling Triton to keep them in registers; also hoist `x_batch_base + ic*H_IN*W_IN` outside the kh/kw loops.
- Switch output store to use `out_off` in NHWC-ish flat form and ensure `offs_hw` is the contiguous (fastest) dim — already true; but consider tiling `(oh, ow)` as a 2D tile (e.g. BLOCK_OH=8, BLOCK_OW=32) so input rows are reused across kh, cutting global loads roughly 3×.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM im2col conv: one program per `(N, BLOCK_M of OC, BLOCK_N of HW_OUT)` doing a `tl.dot` over K=C_IN*KH*KW=72. With K=72 padded to 96 or 128, `tl.dot` on tensor cores will dramatically outperform the current outer-product accumulation in fp32 CUDA cores. Fuse bias-sub-Mish in the epilogue exactly as today.
- Use a 2D spatial tile (BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW, e.g. 8×32) instead of a flat HW tile so that loads of the input patch share rows across kh and columns across kw, increasing data reuse and reducing global memory traffic by ~KH×KW.
- Consider channels-last (NHWC) input layout — permute once at the model boundary — so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous and loads coalesce naturally; weight can be pre-packed to `[C_OUT, KH, KW, C_IN]` at init from the existing `nn.Conv2d` parameters (no algebraic shortcut, just layout).
